newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea steps in to limit won's fall vs dlr.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea steps in to limit won's fall vs dlr.

text.p: The central bank of Korea intervened in the interbank market in late morning trading on Monday to slow the won's decline versus the dollar, dealers said.
But the bank denied stepping into the market, as it routinely does.
Dealers said the central bank began dumping dollars when the won fell to a morning low of 845.20.
They said the demand for dollars have been strong on expectations of large import settlements and the dollar's firmness against the Japanese yen in international markets.
Without further central bank support, the won is seen falling back again, traders said.
The won was trading at 844.60 in late morning trading.
